note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: France: violent protests Monday (worst unrest in years), Macron urges calm; revenue vote Tue Oct 20, Moody's Fri Oct 23; OAT-Bund ~140bp. FY26 deficit $1.992T (5-yr high, ~6.2% GDP). Graham waiver stands — bipartisan backlash, no reversal.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US session: tech rebound (Nasdaq +1.25%, S&P +0.5%) after Friday's -2.15% rout; earnings week ahead (TSLA, META Wed). China Q3 GDP 4.5% beat — retail +1.1% the standout; USD/CNH 6.6811 (strongest since Jun 2022). This week: UK labor Tue 1am CT, UK CPI Wed 1am CT, NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT, PMIs Fri. Tonight: PBoC LPR (hold expected).
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: Canada Sep CPI 3.1% vs 3.2% fc — mild miss. Hot US week stands (CPI 3.7%, PPI 1.3%, imports +8.1% y/y). Eurozone 3.8% confirmed. Brent ~$108.3 (-1.4%), WTI ~$100.4. Wed: UK CPI 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%), NZ Q3 CPI 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y vs 4.1%). Fri: Japan national CPI.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: Warsh: won't prejudge October — December (~89-92% hike) the debate; Oct hold ~84-85% (CME FedWatch); blackout to Oct 29. ECB Oct 29 hold priced (70/73 poll), December the live meeting. BoC Oct 28: ~1-in-4 after the CPI miss. UK Nov 5 ~95% (CPI fc 3.4% Wed). RBNZ Oct 28 two-way (NZ CPI Wed). BoJ Oct 29-30: Oct ~25%, Dec ~80% (Ueda 'quite close'; IMF: may need to tighten faster). RBA Nov 2-3: ~30% (Q3 CPI Oct 28).
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). Crowded trades are fragile: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: No new COT until Friday. Funds net LONG AUD (79th pctile) — squeeze thesis broken; the pain trade is down. Dollar 54th, euro 44th, yen 67th, franc 41st, CAD 31st — none crowded (CFTC TFF, Oct 6).
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Risk-on Monday: tech rebound after Friday's rout (VIX ~20). Sunday's two fears fizzled: no signed Iran deal (talks stalled), no Hezbollah retaliation — haven bid sheathed. Trump waived Russia sanctions Friday → Brent -$1.5 to ~$108.3. Putin floated a Trump-Xi summit; US resumed Ukraine intel sharing. France unrest = the euro's first domestic headwind in days.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent ~$108.3 (-1.4%), WTI ~$100.4 (+1.3%); spread ~$8 — tanker-risk premium, ~2x normal. Trump cut a diesel export deal with Russia (sanctions waiver). Petersburg terminal fire confirmed (FP-1 strike, ~1 killed); damage unquantified. GDT dairy Tue; NZ trade deficit NZ$1.97B (fuel +96% y/y, price-driven).
tot.title: Terms of trade
